claims.claim: Reviewers note that reloading weapons requires physical interactions like inserting magazines and chambering rounds rather than pressing a reload key.

citations.review_text:
This game is the peak of VR role playing and first person shooter. Absolutely flawless, exciting combat and panic inducing reload mechanics, this game really makes you look around and appreciate even the simple details... honestly sometimes this game looks more realistic than the room i am playing in. Its insane! The glove mechanic ends up feeling so natural, you will reflexively try to snap grab items off the counter. 

This one should not be missed if you are playing with a VR headset.

A *must have* for fans of the Half-Life series. Having headcrabs crawling all over you instead of all over your PC's screen is a life-changing (or at least pants-changing) experience.

With a hefty dose of humor mixed with prolonged scenes of crawling through spooky, zombie infested sewers, this is "Ravenholm on steroids".

Bribe, beg, steal or borrow, I don't care how you get the VR set to play this (wait, I'm getting radio communication from Gordon Freeman. He's saying: "Don't steal!"). Don't play it without VR, it would suck.

The controls are extremely tactile -- you won't be just pressing some "R" key to reload your guns, you will be actually loading the magazines and chambering the rounds. You can carry two utility items such as grenades or health injectors, which creates very interesting choices.

This is the first Half-Life game where the protagonist speaks. Wisely, the developers toned down the monologuing to a minimum and most of Alyx has to say will be an actual conversation - typically over a radio - with someone else. That's where Russel (the guy in the ushanka hat) comes in. Russel is an "Asperger-as-hell" weirdo whose brain is operating on a whole different level, creating hilarious misunderstandings and fun exchanges.

In a way, Half-Life Alyx is a showcase of how amazing VR games can be. Every chapter brings something spectacular to the table. Whether you are moving through a space where making a sound can be your death, and so you need to cover your mouth (!!), or whether it's really dark and your tiny flashlight is working overtime, you will be surprised over and over again.

Took me 18 hours to finish my first playthrough on EASY difficulty (with the scale being STORY-EASY-NORMAL-HARD). Now on my third playthrough with Developer Commentary ON.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the multitool puzzle segments as boring.

citations.review_text:
In my decades of gaming life, I can remember only two other games this impressive: the original Doom and Half-Life. Both of them delivered a new experience I did not imagine possible, and Alyx is the third one. 

This game is not perfect. The puzzles with the multitool are generally boring (yes, I know they are meant to help you get used to VR, but still…), and certain gameplay elements are old FPS formula from the Half-Life 2 days. 

However, these shortcomings are really nothing compared to the unforgettable experience. This is not only the best VR game available but another Valve masterpiece that can stand together with the other Half-life and Portal games. I won’t be able to forget the moment at the beginning when a Strider passed over me. 

This game alone is a good enough reason to buy a VR headset. Yes, it’s that good.
The benchmark for all other VR games. It ran very smoothly on my PC and was a blast to play. The door opening puzzles get a bit boring, but everything else about the game is top.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features workshop mods which add extra content and extend replayability.

citations.review_text: truly a masterfull vr game, gameplay is good and simple, graphics are out of this world and it runs even better. its an amazing addition to the half life franchise and overall a great experience. sadly there is almost nothing like this experience and will leave you aching for more. luckily there are loads of workshop mods though.
The best Triple AAA VR game I have ever played on Meta Quest 3 and I love it, get it for a awesome story, experience, and modding.

Have seen half-ilfe games for a while, never played,  just got it due to getting a meta quest,  game on sale  and my dog groomer recommending it,  NOT DISSAPONTED,  really is a good game,  so much to explore and see in the world, graphics and gameplay are awesome, it does put  my system to work though,  replayability is high, you wont be dissapointed.

Immersion so good you'll forget what reality looks and feels like. With suitable haptics for every touch, you can get lost in City-17 like it was your own hometown. You'd be missing out if you played with the no VR mod, as you can genuinely feel every shot you take at an enemy combine, zombie, or antlion. If you have a VR headset, this is a must-buy. Not to mention, it has a thriving workshop scene, so if you've ever dreamt to be Alyx Vance using a bow to shoot an explosive barrel with headcrab zombies crowding it, you can! Honestly, I can't recommend this game enough, you can tell a lot of love was put into this game, and if you still aren't convinced, may I add that it has gnome chompski? That loveable gnome that you carried through the streets of left 4 dead 2 and white forest from half-life 2 episode 2? Yeah, he's here now, and he's surprisingly not as annoying to carry as a lot of people say, I say this with a gnome run under my belt. Are you convinced yet? Well, you better be once I tell you that there's new friendly faces you'll be meeting, new combine you'll be facing, and new xen flora and fauna you'll be struggling against during your journey. It's honestly so cool how big the worldbuilding is for this game, how every beer bottle has a liquid simulation inside, every animal and plant reacting how they would if you were to see them in real life, and all that with surprisingly low requirements for specs. Might I add that almost every interaction has been accounted for? For example, when you're planning your journey, your companion will react accordingly to what you use as a stand-in for yourself. Now, are you ready to play? Because I would be.
It's very good basically. With the workshop community you would need a long time before you run out of content of any type.
One of my favorite vr games. The mods from the workshop are also quite amazing

Amazing graphics, fun gameplay, but it lacks some replayability. While mods can spice up the game, I wish there was some official special maps. (say a zombie wave, or some puzzle rooms.) Otherwise, amazing game.

I got the Half-Life demo from a CD taped to a magazine. As a big Duke Nukem 3d fan, I loved it. Played the absolute ♥♥♥♥ of that demo. I got the full version eventually when I coiuld afford it and still remember being tripped all the way out not being able to find the section from the demo in the full game. I also lied to my friend about being able to beat it. I used god mode, it was years later I discovered the pools on Xen actually heal you! Half-Life 2, the Episodes, Portal, The Orange Box. Oh man. Valve fanboy right here. Big time. I speed-run HL2 occasionally. It's probably still my all time favourite game. Of course I had to buy VR. Just for this game. Of course I had to buy a more powerful computer to run VR, just for this game. I don't regret a single cent spent and would buy it all again. Where is Half-Life 3!? Probably going to splash out and get the new steam VR headset when it comes out shortly. Maybe they'll release a new game to go with it...

Still the best VR game in 2026 that other games try to mimic and often fail. Max immersion, and adds lore to the Half Life story.

Game eats VRAM though, ran okay back in the day on my GTX 1080 with 8GB of VRAM, but even on the high preset the game uses 14GB of my 16GB with my 7800 XT.

had to upgrade my computer to make it playable but i do not regret for a penny as this game is crazy good. i have never been hooked on VR game as this much.
Bonus is that i got it free with steam index so didnt even need to buy the game technically
